structured_output.summary: Signal already published at P 11.13274 d (Rabtsevich research note); not new.
reasons: The signal is already reported: published_signal gives "P 11.13274 d, Rabtsevich, research note, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22967456". That period agrees with period_days 11.132794 and with fit_period_days 11.1327327 (fit_period_error_days 0.00001153) to within about 0.00005 d, so it is the same signal on the same star. A CTOI must be new, so I agree with the mechanical decision to drop.

Empty catalogue fields do not make it new: exofop_tois and exofop_ctois are empty and the verification record (cross-match of 2026-10-15) finds no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match, but a prior publication of the signal is itself a drop condition.

For the record, the astrophysical evidence does not refute a planet, so the drop rests only on prior publication: pixel_verdict is "on target" (pixel_verdicts_by_sector: S32 SNR 7.9, S98 SNR 19.9, best star TIC 4206066), and both difference-image figures (tic4206066_11.13279_s0032.png, tic4206066_11.13279_s0098.png) show the dip centred on the target pixel with the red best-star marker on the target; triceratops_verdict is "likely planet" with fpp_mean 0.1715, nfpp_mean 0, most_likely_scenario "TP on TIC 4206066", nearby_scenarios_excluded True; planet_radius_earth_radii 2.10 +/- 0.28 with transit_grazing False; secondary_depth_ppm 26 +/- 61; odd_even_difference_sigma 1.13; gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.00965.

The caution "neighbour able to cause dip" is weak: gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip lists five Gaia stars at 45-55" of G 16.9-17.9 needing 34-83% dips, which would not yield a difference image centred on TIC 4206066 in two independent sectors, and nfpp_mean is 0.

Weaker points a reviewer of the published signal may weigh, but that do not change this decision: sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.00342 (depth_ppm_by_sector S98 1185 +/- 88, S6 862 +/- 118, S32 691 +/- 130), though cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.0739 is milder and the products differ in cadence (exposure_seconds_by_sector S98:200 S6:1800 S32:120); stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 5.25 and fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis 1.88 with a poorly constrained fit_impact_parameter 0.507 +/- 0.3070; joint_search_detected False (joint_search_snr 14.8 against joint_search_highest_null_snr 10.9) while other_sector_results (S6 SNR 7.1 vs expected 10.0, S32 SNR 7.6 vs expected 10.4) and the all-sector figure tic4206066_11.13279.png still show the transit in both earlier sectors.

No hold is warranted: released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification is empty, and unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star "110" cannot change the fact that the signal is already in the literature.
